home.metaDescription.message: A book on consumer finance systems: from economics and financial mathematics to software architecture and production code.

home.subtitle.message: Consumer finance systems: from economics to code

home.lede.message: The book follows one consumer loan from application to final settlement and explains everything behind it: why the interest rate is what it is, how the monthly payment is calculated, and why a lending platform needs architectural decisions that ordinary enterprise systems do not.

home.bridge.body.message: Ms. Lan borrows 18,500,000 VND for 12 months at a nominal rate of 18% per year. Starting from that loan, the book explains information asymmetry, the annuity formula, amortization schedules, the true cost of credit, the month-end billing cycle, delinquency, credit scoring, and how all of that becomes entities, transactions, events and batch jobs in a platform of more than twenty modules.

home.aud.dev.d.message: Understand why financial systems look complex, and why most of that complexity comes from economic and legal constraints rather than over-engineering.

home.aud.ba.message: Business analysts, product owners, product managers

home.aud.ba.d.message: Gain enough financial vocabulary to work with stakeholders, and enough technical understanding to write requirements that are implemented correctly.

home.aud.fin.d.message: See how familiar business processes are turned into data, workflows and architectural decisions.

home.aud.new.d.message: A map of the whole landscape: where you stand and what to learn next.

home.journey.read.message: Read from the preface to Chapter 16 to move from fundamentals to production problems. Each chapter has three layers: concept, mechanism and implementation. Readers who do not program can read only the concept layer and still get the full picture.

home.journey.ref.message: Or use the book as a reference: the glossary, the formula appendix, the reference architecture, and calculators for repayment schedules and the cost of credit.

cost.invalid.message: Check the inputs: the up-front fee must be smaller than the loan amount and the term must be 1 to 120 months.

cost.a1.message: Cash flow at period 0 = loan amount minus the up-front fee. Cash flows in periods 1 to n = the scheduled instalment (including the final-period adjustment) plus the fixed monthly fee.

cost.a2.message: The monthly IRR is solved by bisection. APR is the monthly IRR times 12 (no compounding); EIR compounds over 12 periods.

cost.a3.message: How APR must be computed depends on each market's regulation. This is an illustrative tool and does not replace the regulator's prescribed method.

calc.invalid.message: Enter an amount of at least 100,000 VND, a rate between 0 and 100% per year, and a whole-number term from 1 to 120 months.

calc.a1.message: Ordinary annuity: payments at the end of each monthly period.

calc.a2.message: Periodic rate r = nominal annual rate / 12, equivalent to the 30/360 convention.

calc.a3.message: PMT rounded HALF_UP to the dong; interest per period = opening balance × r, rounded HALF_UP to the dong; the final period pays off the remaining balance.

calc.a4.message: Fees and insurance are excluded. Use the cost-of-credit tool to compute APR and EIR with fees.

calc.a5.message: Only monthly payments are supported, because that is the only frequency described in the source material.

tc.note.message: Same method as the repayment schedule calculator: ordinary annuity, r = annual rate / 12, HALF_UP rounding to the dong, final period adjusted. Total interest includes the rounding difference in the final period.

settle.a1.message: The schedule is an ordinary annuity rounded like the repayment-schedule calculator. Outstanding principal is the closing balance of the last paid instalment.

settle.a2.message: Accrued interest uses the 30/360 convention: outstanding principal × annual rate / 360 × days, rounded HALF_UP to whole VND.

settle.a3.message: The prepayment fee is a percentage of outstanding principal. The actual fee and method are set by the contract and by each market's regulations.
